newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to order suspension of Hanwa Bank.
newsitem.headline: Japan to order suspension of Hanwa Bank.

text.p: Japan's Ministry of Finance will order on Thursday the suspension of all businesses of Hanwa Bank Ltd except for deposit withdrawals, a senior MOF official in Tokyo said.
Wakayama-based Hanwa Bank is unable to recover its bad loans and will no longer be able to operate as a going concern, the official said.
He said that a clearing bank will be set up by the MOF to oversee its remaining operations and its eventual liquidation.

The regional bank, which operates mostly in western Japan around the city of Osaka, would be the first bank to come under a government suspension order since World War Two, Japan's leading financial daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun reported.

In New York, the dollar dipped under 111 yen on the back of the wider US trade deficit but then recovered to 111.70 yen after the news on speculation that the MOF would push interest rates lower to help Japan's struggling financial institutions.
The MOF, the Bank of Japan and Hanwa Bank were all to have separate press conferences in Tokyo on Thursday morning.
The MOF official said once the suspension has been ordered, Hanwa will reliquish all business and operating rights to the government-established clearing bank.
He said the the MOF will take all necessary steps to protect the rights of all depositors to the bank.
Hanwa Bank, established in 1941, features high ratios of individual depositors and housing loans, according the Japan Company Handbook, published by the financial publisher Toyo Keizai Inc.
